output.brief:
Last week's 5xx rate (0.41%) is within the service's normal range. Over the preceding 26 weeks the mean was 0.354% and the upper normal edge was 0.482%. Three earlier weeks were higher and were investigated with no fault found. The burn rate was 0.82x, well under the 2x page threshold. Bookings did not drop and there were no complaints. The dashboard counts match the raw logs, so this is not a counting artefact.

The "new pods error at twice the rate" finding is a rollout warm-up effect. Every recent rollout, including a config-only redeploy of an unchanged image, shows new pods erroring more while their caches fill. That accounts for only about 10–20 errors, against a rise of roughly 2,300. It says nothing about v4.18 itself.

I can't rule out v4.18, the replica move or partner-sync month-end traffic as small contributors. I'm fairly sure nothing here justifies action.

Next steps: don't roll back, and don't mute alerting, since that would remove protection for no gain. Note the week at ops review and apply the standard check to the following week. If this week exceeds the band, investigate then.
